How I Work

End-to-End UX Process

A structured, adaptive loop — not a waterfall. Click any stage to see what happens inside it, including real examples from the projects above.

01
Discovery & Stakeholder Alignment
Before any design work, I spend time in the problem space — facilitating workshops, mapping organizational dependencies, and aligning on success metrics.
Stakeholder InterviewsBusiness RequirementsSuccess MetricsProject Charter
At Brightspeed, discovery involved 15+ contact center stakeholders across 3 time zones. Running structured facilitation sessions using a modified Jobs-to-be-Done framework surfaced 23 distinct pain points before a single wireframe was drawn — preventing 3 major scope changes worth 6+ weeks of rework.
02
User Research & Behavioral Insight
Contextual inquiry, moderated testing, surveys, and AI-assisted synthesis. I transform data into design decisions that stakeholders can commit to.
Contextual InquiryUsability TestingAI SynthesisJourney Mapping
For Smart Licensing, research with 40+ enterprise admins revealed the key insight: users weren't confused by the data — they were confused by the absence of a shared vocabulary. That single finding restructured the entire information architecture.
03
Information Architecture & Ideation
Card sorting, tree testing, and structured ideation with cross-functional teams. IA decisions are based on evidence, not intuition.
Card SortingTree TestingTask Flow MappingDesign Sprints
The B2B Console IA was validated through card sorting with 12 actual Cisco partners across 4 countries. Partners think by geography and product line — not Cisco's internal API naming. This restructuring reduced primary workflow time-on-task by 40%.
04
Interaction Design & Prototyping
Lo-fi sketches through high-fidelity Figma prototypes. I use prototyping as a thinking tool — every interaction state is considered before a developer sees it.
Lo-fi WireframesFigma PrototypesInteraction Specs7 Iteration Rounds
For Brightspeed's AI Agent Assist, I prototyped 7 distinct patterns for surfacing AI suggestions during live calls. Testing with 50 agents revealed the quietest, least interruptive pattern was most effective — the "invisible intelligence" principle.
05
Design Systems & Token Governance
Token governance, component documentation, and team onboarding are as much my deliverable as the screens. Systems thinking is the multiplier on all other design work.
Design TokensComponent DocsFigma Auto-layoutWCAG 2.1 AA
At Cisco, the design token framework I established became reference standards across the entire design organization. The Figma auto-layout system I built for CCW Renewals accelerated developer handoffs by ~35%.
06
Testing, Validation & Measurement
Usability testing, accessibility audits, and post-launch measurement. I stay involved through engineering delivery — design decisions made in conversation are better than those made in silence.
Usability TestingAccessibility AuditDev Handoff ReviewPost-launch Metrics
Post-launch UAD satisfaction moved from 52% to 97% over 90 days, tracked via a pulse survey embedded in the platform. The 45% improvement was the accumulation of 50+ small decisions throughout the process, each reducing one specific friction point.

AI in Practice

AI Workflows at Brightspeed

How I used AI — not as a gimmick, but as a force-multiplier at every stage of the contact center redesign. Real tools, real outputs, measurable outcomes.

Brightspeed's UAD project ran at enterprise speed with lean UX coverage. I integrated AI tooling into research synthesis, interaction design, QA, and knowledge management — compressing timelines without sacrificing rigor.

The result: a 45% agent satisfaction lift delivered in 90 days, with AI accelerating every phase from discovery to launch.

AI Tools Deployed
Claude AI ChatGPT Gemini Maze AI Figma AI Notion AI Dovetail Otter.ai Midjourney
Design Philosophy
"AI handles the volume. I handle the judgment."
Every AI output was validated against real agent behavior before it shaped a design decision.
🔍
Workflow 01
AI-Accelerated Research Synthesis
Conducted 18 contextual interviews across 3 agent cohorts. Used Claude + Dovetail AI to cluster 340+ raw observations into 23 ranked pain points in hours — not weeks. Sentiment tagging and theme deduplication ran automatically, freeing me to focus on insight judgment.

Agent Assist Pattern Design
Designed the real-time AI suggestion layer surfaced to agents during live calls. Prototyped 7 interaction patterns using Figma AI for rapid variant generation. Tested all 7 with 50 agents via Maze AI — discovered the quietest, least-interruptive pattern won. Named it "invisible intelligence."

About Me

The Person Behind the Work

My design career began in 2005 with a simple HTML/CSS website and a curiosity that never quieted. Over two decades, that curiosity took me from web design in Hyderabad to enterprise UX architecture embedded inside Cisco's global commerce teams — designing systems that thousands of administrators and millions of end users depend on every day.

What I've learned is that the most important design work happens before anyone opens Figma. It's the clarity of a shared mental model, the discipline of a governance process that travels across teams, and the trust built in rooms where design has to earn its place alongside engineering timelines and business roadmaps.

I'm drawn to complexity — not because it's impressive, but because making the complex feel simple is genuinely hard, and that difficulty is where the most meaningful design decisions live.

My Design Philosophy

Design is infrastructure before it is aesthetics. A design system that travels, a research practice that informs product strategy, and a governance process that survives handoffs — these create more lasting value than any individual screen, no matter how beautifully crafted.

Case Study 03 · Cisco · Smart Licensing Analytics · 9-Year Engagement · 2013–2022
Cisco Smart Licensing Platform
Building the single source of truth for enterprise license management — entitlements, consumption, renewals, and compliance — across a 9-year embedded engagement inside Cisco's global commerce teams.
The Problem & Real Product
Cisco's licensing ecosystem connected marketing, finance, provisioning, and customer support — but with no unified analytics view.

Enterprise administrators managing 113K+ Smart Accounts and 565K user accounts had no single place to see license entitlement, consumption, and renewal status. Support tickets went unresolved for weeks because no one could trace a case across disconnected systems.

The cost wasn't just user frustration — it was measurable support overhead, delayed renewal revenue, and compounding design debt across 4 product cycles.
cisco.com · Smart Licensing · Entitlements Overview · Production
My Role

Lead UX Designer — embedded within Cisco's Smart Licensing product team across 4 major product cycles (2013–2022). End-to-end ownership spanning UX strategy, information architecture, interaction design, design system governance, and post-launch measurement. I ran all research, owned IA and interaction design, and led design reviews with 15+ cross-functional stakeholders including engineering leads, product owners, finance, and compliance teams.

UX Process
1
Cross-functional Research (40+ admins)
2
System Dependency Mapping
3
Shared Vocabulary Workshop
4
Unified Analytics IA
5
Iterative Prototype Testing
6
4 Major Product Cycles

The critical research insight: users weren't confused by the data — they were confused by the absence of a shared vocabulary across teams. "Entitlement" meant different things to finance, provisioning, and support. Establishing a shared glossary became the prerequisite to any interface design — and that glossary, documented as part of the design system, outlasted multiple product cycles.

Licensing Analytics — Smart Accounts by License · Real Production
cisco.com · Licensing Analytics (alpha) · Smart Accounts by License

The Smart Accounts by License view — one of the most complex IA challenges in the project. 53,241 smart accounts needed to be navigable by license type (Smart, Classic, EA), entitlement consumptions, and distributor hierarchy simultaneously. The stacked bar visualization and filterable table emerged from 6 rounds of co-design sessions with actual Cisco account managers and SA admins across Americas, EMEAR, and APJC theaters.

Products Analytics — License Lifecycle View · Real Production
cisco.com · Licensing Analytics · Products Overview · Ordered / Entitled / Consumed

The Products analytics view unified three previously disconnected data streams — Ordered (2,039 Smart / 1,019 Hybrid / 3,139 Classic), Entitled, and Consumed — into one coherent lifecycle view. The Smart/Hybrid/Classic donut charts and the tabbed filter (All / Smart / Classic / Hybrid) were validated through 8 usability tests with Cisco partner administrators across 4 geographies. The product table with Purchased vs Consumption columns directly replaced a 47-minute-per-week manual spreadsheet process.

The 9-Year Advantage

A 9-year embedded engagement creates design advantages that project-based work cannot. I understood organizational dependencies, political dynamics around system integration, and Cisco's platform architecture at a level that let me propose solutions others couldn't — because I knew which constraints were real and which were negotiable.

The Smart Licensing redesign was the fourth major iteration I led, each informed by longitudinal research with the same user populations and genuine understanding of how their needs had evolved over time. The Comments module (built for collaborative case resolution) emerged directly from observation of how account managers were working around the lack of a shared notes system — using email threads to track pending issues.
